one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events land on the same day: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-28 (7:30am ET) and the FOMC decision that afternoon. 2026-10-31 is a Saturday, so the 10/30 close settles it. Correction from round 1: the CEO's 'very strong 3Q orders' and '20 GW 2H likely conservative' remarks came at Laguna on 2026-09-16 (stock +4.8% to ~$925), not 10/1; the 10/1 +3.9% move followed Evercore raising its 2027-28 estimates 3-4%. So the strong-orders signal is already in the price twice over. Skeptic points for the print: the CEO said Electrification data-center orders fall from ~40% of segment orders in 1H to ~20% in 3Q-4Q, and most new slot/contract adds land in 4Q, so the 3Q orders headline could look lumpy. EPS consensus is ~$4.07-4.17 after a big Q2 miss ($2.47 vs $3.22); 2H FCF is mechanically weak after a $9.9B 1H. On rates: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 with one more hike signalled, but Polymarket moved to 60% 'no change' for October after soft core PCE (9/30). Credit (Fitch A-), insiders and litigation give no near-term catalyst. Net: no directional edge; median ~$990, ~15% monthly vol (52%/3.5), roughly symmetric in log space.

fair_value.method: Blend of 30x 2028E EPS $31.50 = $945 (40%), 24x 2028E EBITDA $10.2B plus $10.3B net cash over 260M shares = $981 (35%), and a 3.5% yield on ~$8.8B normalised FCF = $967 (25%); weighted ~$963, about 2.5% below the $987.45 close.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E EPS $31.50 x 30x (de-rated from ~40x 2027 consensus today); unchanged from round 1

inputs_detail.derivation: Bottom-up from management's 2028 outlook: $11.2B EBITDA less ~$1.3B D&A plus ~$0.3B net interest income, taxed at ~21%, = ~$8.1B net income / ~258M shares = ~$31; set at $31.50, at the low end of the $30.5-34.8 consensus range because consensus 2028 revenue ($61B) already runs ~9% above management's own $56B outlook and GLJ argues 2027-28 deliveries carry older-vintage pricing; Laguna (source 40) confirms the larger 2026 change in margin in backlog mostly delivers in 2029-30, so it does not lift 2028 EPS, which supports staying at the low end

Today ~40x 2027 consensus ($987.45/$24.91); bears (GLJ, SA Sell, ts2 '40x cash flow') say the premium is cyclical. 30x is my base-case expected multiple, not a bear haircut: the bear scenario separately uses ~20x, so the two do not double-count. I considered moving to 31-32x after the supervisor's double-counting point but held 30x because the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 with another hike signalled (source 42), a modest multiple headwind

2026 FCF is inflated by down payments (contract liabilities +$14.1B in 1H26; 2H26 implied only ~$2B), and management's >= $24B 2025-28 floor implies >= ~$8.3B for 2027-28 combined. Raised from $8.5B because at Laguna the CEO said the change in progress balances is still smaller than the change in margin in backlog, i.e. cash booked is less than incremental profit booked, which tempers the unwind; still anchored near 2028E net income (~$8.1B) plus modest working-capital help

~29x FCF, a premium-industrial yield and above today's ~2.5% (ts2: 40x cash flow); A-/tight spreads (+45-78bp) mean no balance-sheet discount. As with the P/E, this is the base-case yield; the bear scenario's deeper de-rating is separate

bear.story: GLJ-style outcome: 2026 proves the order peak (WoodMac), 2027-28 deliveries carry older-vintage pricing (the CEO himself says the 2026 margin-in-backlog step-up mostly delivers in 2029-30) so EBITDA lands ~$8B in 2027; the January 2027 call shows a 2027 FCF step-down toward the >= $8.3B 2027-28 floor; data-center orders stay lumpy (Electrification DC share falling to ~20% in 2H26) or hyperscaler capex growth stalls; the Fed keeps hiking; Wind keeps losing money; the multiple compresses to ~20x EPS of ~$29 plus ~$40/share net cash. Not a balance-sheet or fraud story: credit is A-, insider selling is token.

base.story: Orders stay strong (backlog >$200B early 2027, 116+ GW under contract), the January call shows a 2026 margin-in-backlog change larger than 2025's low double digits, margins track toward 20% in 2028, and the spring-2027 CMD sets a 2030 outlook; but the stock de-rates from ~40x to ~30x forward in a higher-rate backdrop as order growth decelerates and FCF normalises. EPS growth roughly offsets de-rating for a mid-single-digit gain.

bull.story: AI power supercycle persists, pricing on 2025-26 vintage backlog drives Power margins above 20%, the spring CMD sets 2030 targets well above consensus, Wind turns, services compounds; multiple holds ~38x on ~$38 2028 EPS (Guggenheim $1,450 street high; Evercore $1,350 and 2-7% above consensus through 2028).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$640 (-35%, ~20x 2028E EPS of $31.50, a no-premium peer multiple, and near the lower part of the 52-week range) the move would most likely reflect a fundamental break: slot reservations (63 of 116 GW) failing to convert or being cancelled, the January 2027 margin-in-backlog disclosure stalling, a hyperscaler capex pullback hitting Electrification and gas orders, or evidence that 2027 Power margins are as thin as GLJ argues, rather than ordinary 52%-vol noise. Credit, litigation and insider activity are not plausible break triggers on current evidence. Note the 9/14 close of $874.76 on GLJ's initiation shows a single-day -8.6% move is within normal noise for this name.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact checks changed three inputs and my calendar, not my thesis. (1) Net cash is $10.3B (10-Q: cash $13.12B less borrowings $2.849B; I verified the note table directly); my $3.72B debt included $0.87B operating leases. (2) I read the Laguna transcript (2026-09-16) myself: the 2027 outlook and the 2026 margin-in-backlog change come on the January 2027 call, the CMD with a 2030 outlook is in spring 2027, and there is no December update; my round-1 Morgan Stanley date (10/1) was wrong, and the 10/1 +3.9% followed Evercore's 3-4% estimate raise. (3) The CEO said progress-payment growth is smaller than margin booked, so I raised normalised FCF from $8.5B to $8.8B. But the same transcript says the 2026 margin step-up mostly delivers in 2029-30, which supports the skeptic view that 2028 EPS sits at the low end of consensus, so I kept $31.50. I verified the 9/16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% with one more hike signalled; Polymarket then moved to 60% 'no change' for October after soft PCE, so I treat rates as a modest headwind and use it to hold 30x rather than raise it. On the supervisor's double-counting question, I disagree in part: 30x and 3.5% are my base-case exit multiples, and the bear scenario applies a separate, deeper 20x, so de-rating is not counted twice in the fair value. Methods now: P/E $945, EV/EBITDA $981, FCF yield $967, blended $963 (from $953); scenario mean ~$1,051. Skeptic checks still stand: Fitch A-, ~$11.5M of insider sales, Vineyard Wind settled, short interest 3.3%, and no new short report or downgrade since GLJ (searched to 10/1). Ladder: lognormal median ~$1,000 at ~46% vol with a slightly fat left tail; P(>=987) unchanged at 0.515; the far upper tail trimmed a little for the rate backdrop. One small disagreement with the supervisor: 1H26 buybacks were 4.3M shares for $3.645B (10-Q), about $848 a share, not ~$918; it does not change my numbers. Street mean target $1,237 is treated as evidence of optimism, not the answer.
